title: R1-s entity safety (1): one info_intermission camera in every Quake 1 map
cause: Every Quake 1 map gets exactly one info_intermission (D8 PlacementRole intermission; classname from data/profiles/q1/generator-current.json) at a standing-eye viewpoint over the floor of its largest room, clear of solids and at least 64 units (x or y) from every other entity, with a mangle (pitch yaw 0) facing the room centre.
hypothesis: When a Quake 1 level or match ends, FindIntermission takes an info_intermission, else an info_player_start, else a testplayerstart, and otherwise calls objerror 'FindIntermission: no spot', a fatal Program error (1996 id1 progs FindIntermission statements 5672-5715, reached from execute_changelevel statement 5878; quake-rerelease-qc quakec/client.qc:135-168 and quakec_ctf/client.qc:191-221). Generated Q1 deathmatch, duel, CTF and TDM maps have neither entity, so a fraglimit or timelimit ending is fatal; single-player and co-op maps fall back to the player start's view. Adding one info_intermission removes the fatal path and gives every map a deliberate end-of-level view, and changes nothing else.
expected_mechanism: src/entities.cpp EntityAllocator::populate appends one intermission placement after the lights when spec.game == quake1 and the switch is on (add_quake1_intermission: rooms by floor area, then height, then id; candidate points at 12/88 % corners, then wall midpoints, then the 8 x 8 spawn grid; first point whose standing column x/y +-16 from the walkable surface to eye + 16 lies inside the room, overlaps no solid and no entity volume, and is >= 64 u on x or y from every point entity). Origin z = walkable surface + 46 (player hull mins z -24 plus view_ofs 22; execute_changelevel sets view_ofs '0 0 0' and setorigin to the spot, so the camera is the origin). Yaw faces the room centre, pitch looks at the centre of its floor. src/map_builder.cpp writes classname info_intermission, mangle '<pitch> <yaw> 0' (execute_changelevel copies mangle into angles and v_angle) and origin. No other placement, solid or random draw changes; Q2 and Q3 are untouched (the builder refuses a non-Q1 camera).

declared_scope.description: Written before any run with the new binary (out/phase2/changes/r1s-q1-intermission/declared_scope.json, scripts/declare_scope.py): every non-sealed case whose baseline-0 report resolves game quake1. That is the 142 BENCH-v1 cases of the six Q1 paths (q1-sp 27, q1-coop 23, q1-dm 28, q1-duel 21, q1-tdm 20, q1-ctf-threewave 23); no portfolio case (all Quake 2). Manifest game and resolved game agree for every case.
declared_scope.case_ids_rule: BENCH-v1 ids containing 'q1-' (equal to the declared list, checked by scripts/compile_on.sh)

scope_diff.identity_field_discount: compare.py a738936 counts a switched run's identity fields ($.switches and every layout_sha256) as differences (docs/CHANGE_PROTOCOL.md, known gap). The on-run was normalized by out/phase2/changes/r1s-q1-intermission/scripts/normalize_switched.py, which removes exactly the one switches line and resets the on-run layout hash (5-7 layout_sha256 fields per report) to the off-run's, copying every .map unchanged; the unmodified compare.py then diffed everything else. The raw comparison was kept: 268 BENCH-v1 and 49 portfolio cases out of scope, every one differing only in report bytes at $.switches and *.layout_sha256, with every .map byte-identical (scripts/check_identity_fields.py).
scope_diff.in_scope_difference_shape: every in-scope .map equals its switch-off .map plus exactly one entity block {classname info_intermission, mangle, origin} (142/142); report changes are only counts and lists that grow by that placement: counts.entities, map.stats.entity_count, map.manifest_entries, map.manifest_node_ids, analysis.visibility.summary.placements and segment_tests, navigation placement_bindings (player 142, monster 56); no finding, validation issue, repair, quality, lighting, spawn-safety or timing field changed

evidence_notes: Presence, origin and mangle are read from the compiled BSP entity lumps (compiler output). In-solid and overlap checks are static analysis of the .map brushes and entities. That FindIntermission no longer reaches objerror is static analysis of the 1996 progs disassembly and the re-release QuakeC; no engine was run, so the match-end behaviour itself is not engine-tested (D20 keeps Q1 connected-client tests out).
